business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electron Beam 3D Melting of Porous Titanium Hip Joint Prosthetics

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain has an extensive network of bilateral investment treaties; treaty protection is conditional on the investor's nationality, investment structure, applicable treaty text, and any intra-EU or other jurisdictional limitations.
Spain–United States income tax treaty, signed 1990, as amended by protocol; it is a double taxation agreement, not an investment treaty.
Spain–China income tax treaty, signed 1990; it is a double taxation agreement, not an investment treaty.
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since 2017; investment-protection provisions are not generally in force pending ratification.
The applicable treaty position must be verified against the investor's country of residence and the current official treaty status before structuring.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, particularly Articles 3–4; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May implementing Law 10/2010; Law 11/2021 of 9 July, including tax-transparency and beneficial-ownership-related measures; and Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership. Companies must identify and retain adequate, accurate, and current beneficial-owner information and provide it to competent authorities and the applicable register. Companies Registry filings and beneficial-ownership reporting requirements apply as prescribed by law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, extract from the commercial register, or equivalent evidence of existence of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or public authority in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing country and Spain are parties to the Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization, subject to any applicable treaty exemption

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or other corporate authorization approving the Spanish investment and appointing the signatory or representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The foreign shareholder's competent corporate body; notarization by a competent notary where required by Spanish notarial practice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation, tax registration, and Companies Registry filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or other competent authority in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where applicable; otherwise consular legalization; Spanish sworn translation may be required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document and Spanish tax identification documentation for foreign founders, directors, and identified beneficial owners, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing government authority; Spanish tax identification number issued by the Spanish Tax Agency where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Identity-document authentication depends on the receiving authority and document type; foreign public certificates generally require Apostille or consular legalization unless exempt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial-ownership chart and declaration identifying natural persons who ultimately own or control the company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Prepared and certified by the relevant corporate shareholder or applicant, supported by underlying corporate records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Apostille or consular legalization are required only where the Spanish notary, registry, bank, or competent authority requires them for the particular evidence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Obliged entities under Law 10/2010 must apply risk-based customer due diligence, identify beneficial owners, and apply enhanced measures to politically exposed persons under the statutory rules, including senior-management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds checks, and enhanced ongoing monitoring where applicable. Screen against applicable EU and Spanish sanctions and UN Security Council measures. OFAC screening is not a general Spanish statutory requirement but may be required by US nexus, correspondent banks, or contractual policy. Screen directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories, and relevant counterparties at onboarding and on an ongoing risk-based basis; resolve potential matches before onboarding or transaction execution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online company-name certification service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be distinguishable from names already registered or reserved and must comply with Spanish company-name rules, including Royal Decree 1784/1996 of 19 July (Commercial Registry Regulations) and the rules governing company names. The name must include the appropriate legal-form designation, such as Sociedad Limitada or S.L. Foreign-language wording and foreign characters are subject to registry acceptance; the name must be accurately rendered in the application and must not mislead as to the company's identity, activities, or legal status. A name certificate is required for execution of the incorporation deed.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved company name
Terms implying an official connection with Spain, a public authority, or a public institution without authorization
Terms whose use is restricted or requires prior authorization under applicable legislation, including regulated professional, financial, or public-service designations
Terms that are unlawful, contrary to public order, or misleading as to the company's activities or legal form
Names containing a registered trademark or other protected sign where use would infringe third-party rights
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A positive RMC name certificate reserves the name for six months from issuance, while its validity for execution of the incorporation deed is generally three months; obtain an updated certificate if the deed is not executed within that period. There is no general 30-day reservation period. On rejection, review the stated grounds, amend the proposed name, and submit a new application. Where the refusal is a formal registry decision, seek reconsideration or appeal through the applicable Commercial Registry procedure, including the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública) where available, observing the notification-specific deadline and applicable registry regulations. Obtain Spanish legal advice on the appropriate remedy and deadline before filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish registered office is mandatory under the Companies Act (Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010), Article 9. A virtual office may be acceptable as the registered-office address if it is a genuine address satisfying the statutory connection to the company's effective administration or principal establishment and is accepted for notarial, registry, tax, and service-of-process purposes. A mailbox-only arrangement is inadequate for an implant-manufacturing business. Manufacturing, quality-management, device traceability, storage, and regulatory inspection requirements require suitable operational premises and documented controls.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable statutory or official percentage is published. Unannounced inspections are legally possible, and the practical risk is elevated for a medical-device manufacturer because competent authorities may inspect manufacturing, quality-management, vigilance, and device-compliance arrangements. Premises and records should be inspection-ready.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; excludes contentious work and specialized regulatory submissions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office and compliant premises due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord, service provider, or legal adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; excludes rent, deposit, fit-out, and manufacturing-facility costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Articles 19, 21-22, 62, 66)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil de la Provincia correspondiente (Provincial Commercial Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) followed by mandatory inscription in the Commercial Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid up; the bank certificate of deposit or notarial deposit at the Notary is required before execution of the deed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: In accordance with the Law of Capital Companies and the Corporate Bylaws, the undersigned shareholders, having subscribed and fully paid up the share capital, resolve: (1) to assume the incorporated existence and ratify all acts performed for the formation; (2) to adopt the registered office address stated in the deed; (3) to appoint the sole administrator with the powers and term established in the Bylaws; (4) to authorize the corporate legal representative to execute filings with the Commercial Registry and the State Tax Administration and to open and operate bank accounts; (5) to acknowledge receipt of the settlement of incorporation and registration expenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit electronically to the Registro Mercantil Central a request for a negative certification of the intended corporate name (Certificado de Denominación Social). Provide three alternative names in priority order. The certificate is valid for three months and must be attached to the public deed.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all incorporators (passport or national ID)
Completed name application form (Solicitud de Certificación)
If a foreign company is a founder, admission certificate of the parent company and certified copy of its governing deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, file an administrative reconsideration within one month or apply for a different name; if the certificate lapses, submit a new application and extend validity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Bylaws, Bank Deposit, and Payment of Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish Law Firm and a Notary Public (Notario)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate bylaws (Estatutos Sociales) containing the corporate purpose, registered office, capital breakdown, governance, and administration rules. Open a temporary company bank account in a Spanish bank and deposit the agreed minimum EUR 3,000. Obtain the bank certificate of deposit (Certificado de Depósito) or agree to pay the capital directly before the Notary at the time of executing the deed.
required_dossiers: Draft bylaws signed by all founders
Bank deposit certificate showing full payment of capital
Certified copy of the name reservation certificate from Registro Mercantil Central
Draft of the provisional CIF application data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate is defective or capital is insufficient, correct the deficiency and obtain a new certificate; if the Notary raises a defect in the bylaws, amend the incorporation deed and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) located in the registered office province
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the Notary, execute the public deed of incorporation. Confirm the identity of the incorporators, the corporate purpose, the subscribed capital, the appointed administrators, and the registered office. Sign the deed and receive first copies.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate (valid at execution)
Bank capital deposit certificate or proof of deposit to the Notary
Personal identification and NIF/NIE of all incorporators and appointed administrators
Bylaws previously drafted and accepted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary requires rectification or additional documentation (e.g., updated power of attorney for foreign shareholders), provide the correction within the legal period; if any essential clause violates law, amend the deed and re-execute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT – Spanish Tax Agency)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After execution of the public deed and before registration, present the original first copy of the deed at the AEAT office and complete Form 036 to obtain the provisional CIF/NIF. The provisional code is valid until final registration. Also declare the start of the corporate tax and VAT obligations.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the public incorporation deed
Name reservation certificate (if not yet included in deed)
Form 036 duly completed
Identity of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or identity documentation is missing, submit the missing documents within 10 working days; the provisional NIF will be reissued once the procedural defect is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first copy of the public deed of incorporation with the Provincial Commercial Registry together with the provisional NIF and the completed inscription form (Hoja de Inscripción). Pay the registry fee. The registration generally takes 5 to 15 days. After inscription, the company acquires full legal personality and the definitive NIF is obtained.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the public deed of incorporation
Provisional NIF certificate (Modelo 036)
Name reservation certificate
Bank deposit certificate (already recorded in the deed)
Certificate of trade registry fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar files a defect (motivo de calificación), correct the deed by means of a notarial rectification deed or file administrative appeal against the qualification; the company should promptly address any non-substantive technical observations by supplementary submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Commercial Registry registration is complete, present the registration certificate to the AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF. Register the company and its with directors as employers with the TGSS in the industrial activity code CNAE 3250. Apply for the company’s occupational accident identification number and social security contribution account.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate issued by the Provincial Commercial Registry
Definitive NIF application form (Modelo 036 with updated data)
Public deed and bylaws (certified copies)
Directors’ identification documents
Form TA.1 and TA.7 for employer registration with TGSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of mismatch between provisional and final data, re-submit Form 036; if TGSS rejects or delays due to incomplete employer documentation, furnish corrected employment and address data within the 10-day deadline set by the authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS) – Spanish Medicines and Health Products Agency
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturer Authorization for Medical Devices (Spanish transposition of EU Medical Device Regulation 2017/745, Real Decreto 437/2002 as amended) – required prior to placing the device on the market

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) / Competent Environmental Authority of the Autonomous Community where the facility is located
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) under Ley 21/2013, Annex I, Group 6 (Industrial Installations) for metal production with titanium processing; if only 3D additive manufacturing with no primary smelting, the project may qualify as Annex II, subject to screening per Annex III
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Royal Decree 817/2015 for urban wastewater, Directive 98/83/EC, and Directive 2008/50/EC for air quality; VOC emission limits under Directive 2010/75/EU (VOC threshold 5 t/yr); HEPA H13 filtration for titanium particulates; Hazardous waste categories 06, 08, and 10 subject to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 repeated background; cooling water discharge temperature not exceeding 5°C above receiving body

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification via fire authority inspection under Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE DB-SI) and Regulatory Ordinance for Industrial Fire Safety; structural load inspection certificate issued by a collegiate technical engineer; workplace clearance and occupational risk prevention certificate under Ley 31/1995, PRL plan and initial health and safety evaluation; necessary permits from the local municipality (licencia de actividad) for industrial activity in the designated zone.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. The AEAT administers Spanish tax identification, corporate income tax, value added tax, customs-related tax formalities, and the Register of Intra-Community Operators. Certain regional tax administrations administer specific taxes in the Basque Country and Navarre, but ordinary Spanish SL entities outside those territories are administered by the AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish SL obtains a provisional Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) from the AEAT after incorporation documentation is available and obtains the definitive NIF after registration evidence is submitted. The standard procedure is: (1) reserve the company name; (2) execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary; (3) request the provisional NIF using Modelo 036, normally submitting the deed or incorporation documentation, registered office details, articles, identification of directors and shareholders, and powers of attorney where applicable; (4) register the deed with the Commercial Registry; (5) submit the registration evidence to the AEAT and request the definitive NIF; (6) register the applicable economic activities and tax obligations through Modelo 036; (7) register for Spanish VAT where taxable transactions require it; and (8) apply for inclusion in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and VIES activation where intra-Community supplies, acquisitions, or services are expected. Foreign corporate shareholders and non-Spanish directors may require a Spanish NIF; individuals generally use an NIE where applicable, and foreign entities request an NIF through the AEAT or an authorized representative. A non-resident foreign entity carrying on taxable activities in Spain generally requests an NIF and files Modelo 036, appointing a Spanish tax representative where legally required. The NIF must appear on invoices, customs records, tax returns, and other statutory documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box election for an SL. A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person on its worldwide income if tax resident in Spain. Available elections and regimes are transaction- or status-specific and include tax consolidation for qualifying groups, special regimes for mergers and other qualifying reorganizations, the small-entity regime where statutory conditions are met, and other regulated regimes such as the REIT regime, which is generally irrelevant to an orthopedic manufacturing company. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive and can deny deductions, impose income inclusions, or restrict exemption treatment; they do not provide an elective classification change. Tax residence generally follows incorporation under Spanish law, registered office, or effective management in Spain, subject to treaty rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), supplemented by customs duties and import VAT. Spain is an EU Member State and applies the EU VAT Directive framework. The Canary Islands, Ceuta, and Melilla are outside the ordinary Spanish VAT territory and have separate indirect-tax regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold applies to a Spanish-established SL. A taxable person must register before commencing activities or making transactions giving rise to Spanish VAT obligations, normally through Modelo 036. The 21% standard rate applies unless a reduced rate, exemption, reverse charge, zero-rated export treatment, or other statutory rule applies. Separate EU small-business exemption thresholds may apply only where the relevant cross-border scheme and conditions are satisfied; they do not create a general domestic registration exemption for this Spanish SL.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain generally requires compliant electronic records and invoices in legally specified cases, but it does not currently impose universal real-time VAT invoice clearance for all businesses. The Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including entities in the monthly VAT refund regime, large enterprises exceeding the statutory turnover threshold, and VAT groups, to transmit specified invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT, generally within statutory short deadlines. Voluntary SII election is possible subject to the applicable rules. Public-sector electronic invoicing is mandatory for many invoices to public administrations through approved systems. Law 18/2022 creates a framework for private-sector electronic invoicing, with implementation dependent on regulations and phased effective dates. The AEAT's anti-fraud invoicing and billing-system rules, including the VERI*FACTU framework and related integrity, traceability, preservation, and reporting requirements, apply according to their legally effective implementation timetable; they should not be treated as a universal real-time invoice-clearance system. VAT invoices must contain prescribed data, including sequential numbering, issue date, supplier and customer identification and VAT numbers where required, description, taxable base, rate, VAT amount, and applicable exemption or reverse-charge wording. Imports are documented through customs systems and import VAT may be payable at customs or, where eligible, accounted for through the deferred import VAT mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the EU are generally exempt with the right to deduct input VAT, functionally equivalent to zero-rating, where the statutory exporter, transport, and documentary conditions are met. The seller may arrange the transport or the non-EU customer may arrange it, but the required conditions differ and the seller must retain reliable evidence of export and the purchaser's non-EU status where applicable. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt with the right to deduct input VAT when the goods are dispatched to another EU Member State, the customer is identified for VAT in another Member State, the VAT number is valid, transport is evidenced, and the transaction is correctly reported. Services may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT or exempt depending on the place-of-supply rule and service category; offshore B2B services are not automatically treated as exports and require an analysis of customer status, establishment, use and enjoyment, and applicable special rules. Medical devices and orthopedic implants supplied domestically do not automatically qualify for a reduced or zero rate merely because they are used medically; the applicable rate depends on the precise product and statutory classification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration, normally including the MRN and the export-release and exit-results message
Commercial invoice identifying the Spanish supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR, or courier evidence
Proof that the goods physically exited the EU customs territory, including customs exit confirmation or equivalent carrier and customs evidence
Purchase order, sales contract, delivery evidence, and customer identification sufficient to establish the transaction and transport chain
Evidence of payment or settlement, where relevant to corroborate the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory Spanish VAT export document
For intra-Community supplies rather than third-country exports: valid customer VAT identification, transport evidence, and correct EC Sales List and VAT-return reporting
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain generally imposes no universal statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Export proceeds may be collected through ordinary banking channels, subject to bank AML, sanctions, payment-reporting, and documentation controls. A taxpayer must retain invoices, customs records, transport evidence, contracts, payment records, and accounting records for the applicable statutory period, generally four years for VAT assessment purposes, without prejudice to longer commercial, customs, accounting, or anti-money-laundering retention periods. If export exemption is unsupported or incorrectly claimed, the AEAT may assess the underpaid VAT, statutory late-payment interest, and the corresponding penalty, generally calculated under the General Tax Law according to the seriousness of the infringement; VAT-related penalties can commonly range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, subject to statutory qualification, reductions, and aggravating or mitigating factors. Input VAT refunds can be denied or clawed back with interest where export conditions are not proven. False invoices, fabricated customs evidence, concealment, or deliberate VAT fraud may trigger criminal liability where the statutory tax-fraud thresholds and intent requirements are met, including potential imprisonment and fines. Customs violations may additionally result in customs debt, recovery of duties and import VAT, seizure or confiscation, and administrative or criminal sanctions under the Union Customs Code and applicable Spanish law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting in coordination with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOMEX/OIC) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business for capital-movement statistical reporting and foreign investment screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member state with fully liberalised capital and current account convertibility under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Royal Decree-Law 5/2005. Profit and dividend remittance by non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to standard anti-money-laundering due diligence, corporate law documentation, and tax residence certification. No FX surrender constraints, no currency conversion quota, and no Central Bank authorisation required for ordinary current-account transactions. Exceptional balance-of-payment mechanisms apply only to territories classified as non-cooperative jurisdictions for tax purposes, requiring enhanced compliance reporting but not approval for settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio exist for export proceeds. Spanish law does not require repatriation, surrender, or conversion of export receipts to euros. Exporters may retain and settle foreign currency invoices in any freely convertible currency. A balance-of-payments statistical declaration to the Banco de España may be required on a threshold basis for monetary control but carries no conversion obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low for offshore digital EMI platforms without a European Economic Area (EEA) passport; Medium for EEA-authorised electronic money institutions operating under PSD2. Legal constraints: any non-EEA EMI must be licensed or e-money-authorised by the Banco de España or hold a valid passport from another EEA regulator to provide payment services in Spain. Offshore digital EMIs without such authorisation cannot lawfully open an IBAN account, offer multicurrency settlement rails, or execute SWIFT transfers for the Spanish entity. EEA EMIs may provide payment initiation and transaction accounts but cannot issue credit, provide operating loans, or act as a full treasury bank; an SL engaged in high-value medical device manufacturing should use a regulated deposit-taking bank for capital escrow and primary liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish banks generally mandate physical appearance of at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) at the branch during initial onboarding, especially for a non-resident-owned Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL). Remote opening is permitted only in limited circumstances using a qualified digital signature, video identification, and notarial power of attorney; however, the execution of the capital increase deed and company powers often requires physical attendance before a Spanish notary. The practical onboarding viend out as largely in-person for inbound cross-border capital structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Appearance of a foreign shareholder or UBO resident in a high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction triggers enhanced customer due diligence and a material suspension risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate registry extract of the parent, certified passport copies, utility or bank statement for residence proof, personal tax residency certificate (Form 030 or equivalent), organogram demonstrating the ownership chain, business rationale letter, and signed source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial relationship with public hospitals or government-run procurement agencies raises politically-exposed person (PEP) and corruption risk filters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed purchase orders and framework healthcare supply contracts, AEMPS (Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios) medical device registration certificate for ISIC 3250 titanium orthopedic implants, ISO 13485 quality management certificate, tax identification of counterparty, and site-visit or final-beneficiary documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Equity injection mismatched with capital increase deed or transactional profile creates inconsistencies on beneficial ownership and thin-capitalisation review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified notarial deed of capital increase registered at the Spanish Mercantile Registry, BIC/SWIFT reference of inbound transfer, tax Form 720 if applicable, board minutes resolving the capital contribution, bank statement confirming funds received, and explanatory affidavit of the funding chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocols require credit transfers from the foreign shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's operating or capital escrow account using SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details. The transfer must be classified as an equity capital operation and supported by a notarised and registered capital increase deed executed in Spain. Foreign direct investment by EU and non-EU residents is generally free, but if the investor is outside the EU/EFTA and the activity touches strategic sectors (critical infrastructure, energy, transport, telecommunications, dual-use technology, or sensitive medical data), the transaction may need prior clearance under Spanish foreign investment screening (Law 19/2003, amended by Royal Decree-Law 34/2020). The SL must retain the SWIFT receipt, the notarial deed, the Mercantile Registry filing, and a cost-benefit or valuation submission if required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for raw materials, subcontracted machining, and overseas distribution should use SWIFT MT103 for direct documentary credit transfers, Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for sale/purchase with bank assurance, and SWIFT MT700/MT710 as the corresponding LC issuance/advice rails. All outbound payments require matching Spanish customs/export documentation, AEMPS product compliance certificates, the commercial invoice, bill of lading, and if any non-EU sanctions exposure exists, a sanctions screening and dual-use/KYC clearance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on illiquid or emerging-market currencies, not requiring physical EUR settlement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 42% of qualifying expenses); innovation incentives; regional tax benefits in certain autonomous communities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return filed electronically through the Agencia Tributaria portal (www.agenciatributaria.es)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the tax period (e.g. 30 April for a 31 December year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before deductions and incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must report only Spanish-source income; foreign income is generally exempt unless attributable to Spanish permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for R&D and innovation expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim limited deductions if attributable to Spanish operations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax on dividends or other distributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents file to claim treaty relief on outbound dividends

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Administrative fines of €100 to €600 per day of delay; criminal sanctions for evasion including imprisonment; 20% interest on unpaid taxes; potential director liability

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC); submit application to Agencia Tributaria for reduced withholding rate under applicable Double Tax Agreement (DTA); file form 210 for dividend withholding
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory rate, reduced to 0% under many treaties including EU; Interest: 19% statutory, reduced to 0% under EU Interest and Royalties Directive for intra-group

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 20 million consolidated group turnover for mandatory Local File and Master File documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain enforces Economic Substance requirements for entities holding IP, conducting financing or holding activities; non-compliance triggers penalties up to 5% of turnover and potential deregistration

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or failure to file returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines equivalent to 100-150% of evaded tax, imprisonment from 6 months to 6 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable; possible disqualification, restitution, and criminal prosecution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's length prices without supporting documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to 5% of turnover; adjustments to taxable base; interest on additional tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability for tax due; potential criminal liability if fraudulent

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining Spanish entity without sufficient local operations or substance for tax purposes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Deregistration as tax resident; back taxes; fines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for unpaid taxes; possible criminal sanctions under AML and tax laws

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring repatriations to evade reporting or use shell entities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 10% of turnover; criminal charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment, travel bans, and personal restitution obligations
